While foreign investors turned net buyers this month, domestic investors have turned net sellers, largely stepping up for profit booking. Image used for representation | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStock
The story so far: Amid escalating geopolitical tensions, a boom in the AI sector, and valuation concerns, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have been exiting the Indian market for the last two years. However, in a change of course, FPIs have returned to India, and pumped the Indian markets with all-time high inflows of ₹89,856 crore so far in November.
The recent slowdown in AI stocks and concerns about their growth prospects have brought investors seeking a safer bet back to India. The boom in global AI and tech stocks over the last two years prompted investors to move too heavily into tech-heavy countries like the U.S., South Korea, and Taiwan.
